description: Three built-in managers do most of the work here:
github-actions -- the four action refs across .github/workflows/*.yml
and .github/actions/setup-waddle-build/action.yml
mise           -- cmake, ninja and xcodegen in mise.toml, and uv in
.config/mise.toml (the tools no build step runs)
xcodegen       -- ZIPFoundation, pinned in App/project.yml
A fourth, custom regex manager (customManagers below) watches the native
pins in shell scripts, which no built-in manager can read:
Scripts/build-deps.sh     -- SDL_TAG, OPENAL_TAG, SONIVOX_TAG, LIBOGG_TAG,
LIBVORBIS_TAG, LIBSNDFILE_TAG, LIBFLAC_TAG,
LIBOPUS_TAG
Scripts/fetch-freedoom.sh -- FREEDOOM_VERSION
Each pin carries a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=... versioning=...`
comment on the line directly above it, and the one regex reads both lines.
The datasource is per pin because the upstreams differ: github-releases
where the releases page is complete, github-tags for sonivox (publishes no
releases), vorbis (one release, the rest are tags) and opus (releases stop
at v1.5.2 while the pin is the v1.6.1 tag). SDL and opus use regex
versioning because `release-3.4.18` and two-part `v1.6` are not semver;
anything that does not match (SDL's prerelease tags, OpenAL Soft's rolling
`latest` and `utils` releases) is invalid and ignored.
Those updates are NEVER automerged, majors or not. Unlike the tools above,
they are linked into the shipped binary (or, for Freedoom, are the game
data in the bundle), and a green CI run does not show what a new SDL does
on a device. They open one pull request per library, labelled
`ships-in-binary`, with a `build(shipped-deps):` subject, after the same
three-day minimum release age, and wait for CI, the review and the
owner's merge. Merging one ships a TestFlight build. What a bump needs
besides the one line is in Engine/WOOF_UPSTREAM.md, 'Renovate pull
requests for the native pins'; each pull request body links there.
A fifth, pep723, is opt-in (its default file list is empty) and pointed at
Scripts/build-mark.py alone: its inline metadata pins Pillow, and
Scripts/build-mark.py.lock holds that pin's hashes. Renovate edits the pin
but not the script lock, so the pull request goes red at the lock check in
Scripts/test-build-mark.sh until someone re-locks; it is never automerged
(the last packageRule below).
Deliberately NOT watched, and why:
WOOF_COMMIT in Scripts/vendor-woof.sh -- must stay manual. Engine/woof
is a committed tree carrying the iOS patch set, so bumping the SHA
without re-running the script leaves the two silently disagreeing,
and running it wipes the patch set; the move is the three-way merge
in Engine/WOOF_UPSTREAM.md. Upstream also has no SDL3 release tag to
follow, only master.
Engine/woof/third-party (miniz, spng, yyjson, libebur128, ...) -- part
of that committed tree, so they move only with the Woof pin;
ignorePaths below keeps every manager out of Engine/woof.
Nothing else was left out for want of a release stream: every other
pin's upstream publishes tags Renovate can read.
Scripts/check-deps-current.sh stays the weekly report for those two
groups, and still lists the watched pins as well, so a pin Renovate has
quietly stopped matching does not go unseen.
postUpgradeTasks is not an option for a bump that needs a second edit:
the hosted app blocks commands. None of these pins needs one by default
(no committed checksum, fingerprint or cache key), and where a bump does
need more -- an SDL patch that no longer applies, a changed SONiVOX
instrument bank -- the cold CI build fails with the instruction, and a
person or agent pushes the fix to Renovate's branch.
config:best-practices enables digest pinning, so the first run opens a
'Pin dependencies' PR that SHA-pins every action with a trailing
# vX.Y.Z comment -- that PR is what closes issue #16.
Automerge. Low-risk updates merge themselves once the pull request's
checks are green: minor and patch releases, digest and pin moves, and
lock-file maintenance. Majors stay a human decision. Renovate does the
merge itself rather than GitHub's auto-merge (platformAutomerge is off),
because main's ruleset names no required status checks, and GitHub's
auto-merge waits only for REQUIRED checks -- with none, it would merge
the moment the PR opened, CI red or not. Renovate instead waits for
every check on the branch to pass before merging, which is the gate we
actually want. The three-day minimumReleaseAge on those updates is the
supply-chain hedge: a release pulled or re-tagged within days of
publication never reaches main unattended.
The native pins. Reads a `# renovate:` comment and the pin on the
line directly below it; extractVersion is optional and only
Freedoom uses it (the pin is 0.13.0, the tag v0.13.0).
Group all mise-pinned tool updates into one PR. cmake, ninja and
xcodegen are only ever consumed together by a build, and each one
invalidates the same CI caches, so separate PRs would each pay for
a cold build to prove the same thing.
Leave `runs-on: xcode-27` alone. Renovate reads a runner label as
a github-runners dep and would offer a newer one on its own, but
the runner image is pinned in lockstep with XCODE_VERSION /
SIMULATOR_OS, which Renovate cannot see. A runner-only bump lands
on an image that may not ship Xcode 27.1, and setup-waddle-build
hard-fails when the requested Xcode is absent -- so the PR could
never go green on its own. Moving runner images is a coupled,
human decision; drop this rule if that stops being true.
Low-risk updates merge themselves when green. Minor and patch
releases of the actions, the mise tools and ZIPFoundation, digest
and pin moves (what config:best-practices' digest pinning produces),
and lock-file maintenance. A green run here means the engine built,
the unit suites passed and every Scripts/test-*.sh suite ran, which
is the same evidence a human merge rests on. Majors are excluded by
omission and keep needing a review.
The native pins never merge themselves. This rule comes AFTER the
automerge rule on purpose: later rules win, so it turns automerge back
off for minor and patch releases of everything the custom manager
extracts, and applies the three-day age to majors too. One pull
request per library (no groupName): each is a separate thing to test
on a device, and a grouped pull request cannot say which one broke.
The subject is `build(shipped-deps): update dependency <repo> from
<old> to <new>`, and both halves are read by Scripts/whats-to-test.sh:
scope `shipped-deps` puts the bump under 'In the app' in the
TestFlight notes (plain `deps` or type `build` would file it behind
the scenes and tell testers nothing changed), and 'from X to Y' is
where it takes the two versions from. Scripts/test-whats-to-test.sh
pins that shape; change it there first.
prBodyNotes: **This changes what ships.** It is not automerged: it needs CI, an independent review and the owner's merge, and merging it ships a TestFlight build. CI builds every dependency cold for this pull request, so a failure in `Scripts/build-deps.sh` or a `Scripts/check-*.sh` guard is the bump asking for a second edit, and its message says which. See [Renovate pull requests for the native pins](https://github.com/tylervick/waddle/blob/main/Engine/WOOF_UPSTREAM.md#renovate-pull-requests-for-the-native-pins).

description: SDL: stable releases only. SDL gives a development series an odd
minor (3.1.x, 3.3.x) under preview-/prerelease- tags, which the
versioning regex already rejects; this says so in the config as
well, in case one is ever tagged release-. The note below is added
to the general one above (prBodyNotes merges across rules).
prBodyNotes: SDL carries local patches in `Scripts/patches/SDL/`. If the build stops with `applies neither forward nor in reverse`, read the patch's header for the upstream commit it backports: delete the patch if this release contains that commit, otherwise re-base it, and push that to this branch.

description: SONiVOX: the instrument bank is what players hear, and
Scripts/check-eas-bank.sh refuses a release that changed it.
prBodyNotes: If `Scripts/check-eas-bank.sh` fails with `instrument bank changed`, this release altered the wavetable bank. That is a decision about how the music sounds, not a hash to refresh: listen on a device first, and only then regenerate the recorded hashes with `Scripts/check-eas-bank.sh --print`.

description: Freedoom: new game data, so levels, and with them saves and demos
made on the old release, can change.
prBodyNotes: A Freedoom release changes maps, so saves and demos recorded on the previous one may not load, and `App/UITests/Fixtures/` is derived from the old release (its README names the version). Whether players' existing Freedoom saves survive is the owner's call, not CI's.

description: Pillow, pinned in Scripts/build-mark.py's inline metadata (PEP 723).
It draws the app icon's mark, so a release can change committed
artwork, and Renovate cannot regenerate Scripts/build-mark.py.lock:
the pull request needs a person or agent to re-lock and re-render.
After the same three-day minimum release age as everything else.
prBodyNotes: This bumps the Pillow pin in `Scripts/build-mark.py` but not its lock. On this branch run `uv lock --script Scripts/build-mark.py`, then `mise run icons` and `mise run check-icons`, and push the lock with any artwork that changed. Until then `Scripts/test-build-mark.sh` fails at its lock check, by design.
